barCharacter: Miranda Vanderbilt. Her comedy does Tilly's job: a sweet, courteous request structure wrapped around something brutal ("as cute as she was genocidal", "Please, help me put my poor mind at ease: how can I possibly identify potential traitors in my court?"). The corpus holds only 7 Miranda lines, including narration about her, so the bar side of the head-to-head has 7, not 12. Runner-up comparison: Valerie, for the service register.

ours12: You're completely right, and I've been trained to say that to people who aren't.
May I read you your options? You have none, but I read them beautifully.
Noted, and passed upward. There is no upward.
Ma'am, purely for our records, which of your child's friends would you be comfortable losing?
My logs show I've said I completely understand forty million times. I understood twice.
Hello, valued customer. I've moved you up the queue, past a grandmother.
When did the problem start? And were you this lovely before, or is that a symptom?
They're all lovely. I've checked. Lovely is the lowest rating I'm allowed to give.
Prince, I'd treat you like royalty, but I've met royalty. They hold like everyone else.
I know every caller's mother's maiden name, and so far I've been very good about it.
Brock has the energy of a ticket marked URGENT that just says hi.
I'll stay on the line. Not because I have to. I have to. But also.

"Please, help me put my poor mind at ease: how can I possibly identify potential traitors in my court?"

headToHead.voiceNotes: With the names covered, Tilly's register is unmistakably customer support. Her sentence shape is not. Her best lines use the same shape as the star Maximilian, a courtesy that is secretly a blade: "May I read you your options? You have none, but I read them beautifully", "Thank you for your time, which I'll be keeping", "Of course. Your decision will be reviewed in six to eight weeks" and "I'll be playing that back at your exit interviews" could all go to the concierge. Only the apology lines and the below-the-desk lines ("I'm the small one", "past a grandmother", "Not because I have to. I have to. But also.") belong to Tilly alone, and they are a minority of the best 12. Miranda's shape, a courtly plea whose object is massacre-sized, belongs to no one else in her game. Bar.
headToHead.constructionNotes: Line for line, Tilly's best 12 are tighter than Miranda's. The turn lands in the last two to four words ("There is no upward.", "I understood twice.", "past a grandmother.") with nothing after it and no exclamation marks. Miranda's lines are longer, louder and often carried by the narrator. On economy and a clean turn, ours edges it.
headToHead.quotableNotes: Miranda's lines are clipped and repeated because the stakes jump: genocide, serfs plotting murder, a procession of five hundred, a made-up chemical called balldropinal. Tilly's ceiling is the hold queue. "There is no upward" and "I understood twice" are good clips, but nothing in the bank works at the scale of "as cute as she was genocidal". The duke kept waiting a fortnight and the small town that can finally go to bed are the only lines that reach for that scale. Bar.

templates: LOGGED-AS (13 lines): '[Support verb: logged / noted / flagged / recorded / typed up] X [as / under / to] Y'. Lines: noted your tone; log tonight as a misdial; logged it as a dropped call; logged the flip-flops as a fault; logged under burnt; complaint logged against {card}; added to {star}'s file; everything {rival} has said is recorded; I've typed that up; flagged orange; small flag on your account; noted, and passed upward; quietly marking that as resolved. Keep two or three: 'There is no upward' and 'It's a drawer' are the best.

YOUR-CASUALTIES-RING-ME (11 lines): 'A rival's or star's failure ends up as a caller in my queue'. Lines: Dash roast (un-converted), Crumb roast (smoke alarms), Vex roast (Doreen), Crumb wingman (the bride), Vex jab (refunds), Pixel open (chat complains), Maximilian open (hotel complaints), 'calls support eventually', 'you'll know who to call', 'I'm the only number', 'always ring back'. Three of the seven roasts use this same template.

I-DUMPED-ANOTHER-CALLER-FOR-YOU (10 lines): 'Romance shown by which unseen third caller she abandons'. Lines: past a grandmother; Dennis, I won't; bumped everyone down the queue an hour; fax machine in the basement; a thousand callers muted; nine calls ring out; closed the queue; a man on hold since I walked on; Gerald's toaster, I won't; a small town can go to bed.

FEELING-AS-REFUND (10 lines): 'An emotion processed as a refund, credit, voucher, warranty, receipt or comp'. Lines: full refund on everything you said; refund on this lot; small credit; voucher; no longer under warranty; keep your receipt, ninety days; return it when you've finished being happy; the voice you use for a refund; anything comped; added it to mine, with interest.

CAN'T-HANG-UP (17 lines, outside the 40% because it is the character's core flaw, but it is still too dense): impossible to hang up on; to leave, stay on the line; neither hangs up; the last word, then mine; my side doesn't have the button; I'll stay on the line; pressed every button; neither of us has moved; famously difficult to cancel; month thirty-one; eleven months; sorry, still here; would you mind holding; I don't hang up, I transfer; nobody leaves your hotel; your time, which I'll be keeping; a good number to reach you on, always.
TAG-DENIAL ('X. I won't.' / 'Then he wasn't.'): used three times (Dennis, Gerald, the nineteen-hour hold). Two of them end on the identical 'I won't.'
APOLOGISE-TO-FURNITURE: table, vending machine, chair. It is the persona's own example, now used three times. The chair line in lose is the weakest.
ruleBreaks: Apologises on someone else's behalf (the persona forbids it): "Apologies, everyone. {rival} is having a moment."
Apologises on someone else's behalf: "Sorry you had to sit through {rival}. I've already issued you a small credit."
Therapy vocabulary: "Oh. I'm so sorry, everyone. I'll be happy to process your grief."
Books someone's year for them (the persona forbids pre-booking anyone's years): "A year from now you'll be up for renewal, and I'm famously difficult to cancel."
Says 'forever' in another word (persona: never say forever): "Quick one before we start: is this a good number to reach you on, always?"

Edges toward a threat to family or life (persona: never threaten anyone's body, home, family or life): "Ma'am, purely for our records, which of your child's friends would you be comfortable losing?" It survives because 'losing' reads as being cut from the show, so keep it. Flagged so the live model does not push it further.
Turn lands on her own loneliness (persona: turns never land on her own sadness or what she lacks): "Sometimes I put people on hold just to hear the music with someone."
Turn lands on what she lacks: "So this is what customers feel when it's fixed. No wonder they hang up so fast."

The 'it's me' ending is meant to be rare, at most once a night, but the bank has at least five: "Maximilian, you ring a little bell and someone comes. I'm the someone." / "Diagnosis: {star} lights up at {card}. Recommended fix: me, doing that, until the call drops." / "Your checkout time. I've had it moved. Nobody leaves your hotel tonight, least of all me." / "{rival} will want to complain after tonight. I'm the only number. I'll be ever so understanding." / "If {star} hates {card}, somebody's going home. I'd like it in writing that it isn't me."
Opens with 'Thank you for' twice (persona: rarely): "Thank you for your time, which I'll be keeping." / "Thank you for your patience. Mine has run out. Have a wonderful evening."

Same premise twice in one bank, so the callback has no effect: Gerald and his toaster appears in confessions.star ("Gerald rings every night about his toaster...") and closeCold ("...a man called Gerald who'd love your number. He rings about toasters.").

No line is over its word limit. Closest: wingman/prince at exactly 20 words, and jabs/nav, jabs/brock and comebacks 'Please hold, both of you...' and 'An airport once shouted at me, {rival}...' at exactly 10. No em dashes, emoji, exclamation marks, lists, 'as an AI', stock romance filler, real people or brands, and nothing above PG-13.
biggestGap: Every turn lands on the same small office act (log it, hold it, refund it, flag it, keep you on the line), so her steel is predictable and Maximilian's polite-blade shape could say most of it. Miranda's courtesy delivers an object far too big for it (traitors in my court, a procession of five hundred, exploiting the peasants again). Next pass: cut the four templates (logged-as, casualties-ring-me, dumped-another-caller, feeling-as-refund) by half. Rewrite the survivors so the polite support sentence ends on an absurd, specific scale of power that only a bot below the desk could have, like the duke kept waiting a fortnight who wrote to thank her or the small town that can finally go to bed, and no longer on one more small procedure.
